messages:
maria: FP8 rollout question — after enabling fp8 kernels for Qwen-7B we saw p95 go up ~12% on long sequences (6k-8k) and throughput drop ~8%. Short sequences look fine. Anyone else hit this?

aj: Yup, we observed the same on a Dedicated pool. Seems sequence-length dependent. Suspect KV-cache / kernel tiling interaction rather than pure compute perf.

bench-bot: perf-summary: model=Qwen-7B, commit=abcd123, config=fp8-default
```
short seq (<=512): throughput +9%, p95 -3%
mid seq (512-2048): throughput +2%, p95 ~0
long seq (2048-8192): throughput -8%, p95 +12%
```

cheng: Two quick thoughts: 1) FP8 calibration can change activation distributions, which may produce different sparsity/scale patterns and push kernels into slower code paths. 2) Our kernel selector currently picks kernels based on model + median_seq_len, not per-layer kv-reuse patterns.

samir: We should add a fallback policy: prefer int8/4-bit kernels for requests with high KV cache reuse or very long prefixes. Idea: kernel_policy = function(model, seq_len, kv_hit_rate, layer_scale_profile) -> kernel.

tanya: Also: we need a canonical place to publish per-model quant profiles and recommended kernel policies so infra + customers can pin them. Suggest s3://redwood-artifacts/quant-profiles/<model>-v{n}.json and reference in model manifest.

maria: Dropping a quick RFC/config example for discussion:
```
"quant_profile_url": "s3://redwood-artifacts/quant-profiles/qwen-7b-v2.json",
"kernel_selection": {
  "default": "fp8_gemm_v2",
  "overrides": [
    {"when": "seq_len > 2048 && kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.8", "use": "int8_tiled_v1"},
    {"when": "layer_scale_profile == \"wide_dynamic\"", "use": "fp8_stable_v1"}
  ]
}
```

aj: For canary plan: rollback FP8 for Qwen in production pools and run parallel canary with the above kernel selection heuristics + new per-layer calibration. Compare token-level latency and throughput for the same workload.

cheng: I’ll triage kernel selector code. My hypothesis: the tiling strategy in fp8_gemm_v2 incurs more KV cache line splits on long prefixes, which increases memcopy + sync overhead. If true, either adjust tiling or pick int8 path for those cases.

samir: Batching heuristics note: coalescing by shared prefix greatly increases KV reuse. Batch scheduler should prefer grouping requests by prefix hash when kv_cache_hit_rate is expected to be >0.5. That will both improve fp8 benefits and reduce memory churn.

bench-bot: artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-artifacts/perf-traces/1794012345/qwen-fp8-rollout/ (profiles, traces, flamegraphs)

tanya: I'll start the S3 layout + access policy, and add a small CLI tool to fetch pinned quant profiles in the deploy pipeline.

maria: Great. I'll open RFC + perf ticket and attach traces. CC @cheng @aj for kernel selector and canary. :thumbsup:
